finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to URI.open (open-uri) with no validation. An attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary http/https/ftp URLs, including internal services and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is a full-read SSRF. On Ruby versions before 3.0, Kernel#open semantics may also allow more, but URI.open here is already sufficient.
finding.source: HTTP GET /rss query parameter `u` (params[:u]), controlled by any remote client
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read at app.rb:8; the response body is returned at app.rb:9

trace.note: params[:u] passed directly to URI.open, which fetches the URL
First 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned in the response

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, or IP allowlist or denylist. The TRUSTED list is only used in /trusted. No authentication. No private-IP or DNS-rebinding protection.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] directly to URI.open with no validation, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes; the TRUSTED check exists only in /trusted (app.rb:14) and is not applied to /rss.
